newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania central bank to cancel licences of 2 banks.
newsitem.headline: Romania central bank to cancel licences of 2 banks.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) governor said on Wednesday the BNR would withdraw banking licences to troubled private banks Dacia Felix and Credit Bank.

"The BNR will have to apply the final legal sanction which is withdrawing their licences," Mugur Isarescu told reporters after signing a letter of intent for resumption of International Monetary Fund credits.
He gave no further details and did not say when the licences would be rescinded. But he said the banks had failed during a nine-month period to prove they had viable recovery plans.

Last July, the BNR ended months of financial support extended to Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA and Dacia Felix SA, saying further support might fuel "uncontrollable inflationary pressure".
The BNR then turned their files over to courts to determine whether they would be subject to liquidation or reorganisation.
No Romanian bank has been declared bankrupt since the 1989 fall of communism.
Neither of the two banks concerned has conducted any operations on the interbank market for several months and parliament has passed a law entitling the BNR to help redeem their small depositors.

Credit Bank, which ran into trouble after its president was jailed on fraud charges, has launched legal proceedings against the BNR action and a Bucharest court is to rule on the litigation on Friday.

Dacia Felix SA -- once a fast growing bank now struggling with bad debts of some $200 million and a 642.2 billion lei 1995 loss -- has worked out a recovery plan. But it awaits a court ruling in the Transylvanian city of Cluj, its base, on reorganisation or liquidation.
